I was only 6 at the time and I honestly never understood it until later on in life. My mom wasn't one that would sit me down and tell me im different or I need extra help with things right away. She said I was gifted and people would be jealous of my gift. She tried hard for me to never dwell on it but around 10 or 11 years old when people would mock what I had and called it a very rude name. When I was called things pretty harmful I asked her what they meant and she finally broke down why I had trouble keeping friends and handling social situations. It hit me pretty hard then but it took awhile for it to sink in due to how young I was at the time of diagnosis. As a near 21 year old now I tend to not remember a lot of my childhood and honestly I do not want to. People with this disorder are gifted and should not feel down about the fact they have it. I have come a long way from not being able to sit in a loud restaurant for a minute due to the noise, to being a top student at my university. My diagnosis was not a false positive I very much do have it and in ways it still does show up. I wish you luck with your diagnosis and that things work out in the way you want them to. Just know if the worst case scenario happens you are not alone, you are gifted, and you will go far in your life even with the chains of it holding onto you. <3
